title: Supercurrent as a bulk probe for topological phase
authors: Tatiana de Picoli, Ian Wojtowicz, Jukka I. Vayrynen
abstract: Distinguishing trivial from topological superconducting phase remains a central and contested experimental challenge, since most existing probes infer the bulk phase transition indirectly, from boundary signatures that can be sensitive to local physics. Here, we propose an alternative that probes the bulk topological phase and is based on supercurrent response. We study a one-dimensional Rashba spin-orbit-coupled superconducting nanowire with an applied magnetic field that opens a topological gap. We show that for strong spin-orbit coupling, the superfluid stiffness, and consequently the supercurrent, is suppressed by a factor of two inside the topological phase, producing a non-monotonic signature of the bulk phase transition as a function of chemical potential. We further use a low-energy helical model to understand this suppression analytically. Our results show that the bulk topological phase transition can be detected through kinetic inductance measurements.
summary: This paper proposes using the supercurrent response as a direct, bulk probe to distinguish between trivial and topological superconducting phases in nanowires. By analyzing the superfluid stiffness ($ho_s$) in a Rashba nanowire, the authors predict a characteristic non-monotonic suppression of the supercurrent when the system enters the topological phase. This offers an experimental route independent of relying solely on boundary effects.
main_problem: The central challenge is distinguishing between trivial and topological superconducting phases, as existing probes often rely on boundary signatures sensitive to local physics.
main_result: The supercurrent response ($\mathbf{j}_q$) provides a bulk-sensitive probe, showing a predicted factor of two suppression in the superfluid stiffness ($ho_s$) inside the topological phase.
method: The supercurrent and superfluid stiffness are calculated using the Bogoliubov-de Gennes (BdG) Hamiltonian formalism, supplemented by a low-energy helical model for analytical insight.
model_or_system: The system studied is a one-dimensional Rashba spin-orbit-coupled superconducting nanowire subjected to an applied magnetic field. The physics is modeled using the BdG Hamiltonian, which is simplified via a low-energy helical approximation.
key_observables: Superfluid stiffness ($ho_s$), supercurrent ($\mathbf{j}_q$), and the resulting non-monotonic signature of $ho_s$ as a function of chemical potential ($\mu$).
important_parameters: Strong spin-orbit coupling regime ($\Delta < V_x < m\alpha^2$), applied magnetic field ($\mathbf{B}_x$), and chemical potential ($\mu$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the low-energy helical model derived by linearizing the Hamiltonian around the Fermi momentum, and the supercurrent is calculated via expectation values in the BdG framework.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the dependence of superfluid stiffness ($ho_s$) and the dimensionless critical current ($j_c$) on the chemical potential ($\mu$) for different magnetic field strengths, comparing full and helical model results.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the problem with boundary-sensitive probes, proposes supercurrent as a bulk observable, develops the theoretical framework using the BdG Hamiltonian and low-energy models, and finally presents the key result: the non-monotonic signature of $ho_s$ indicating the topological transition.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete, measurable superconducting response (supercurrent/kinetic inductance) that can directly probe the bulk topological nature of a superconductor, which is highly relevant for understanding topological superconductivity in mesoscopic devices.
